correctness.rationale: For a>0 the unique unordered diametral pole pair is proved by the Minkowski-sum triangle inequality. Explicit cap charts give a positive-definite 4-dimensional quadratic deficit with eigenvalues r/4 and ra/[4(a+r)] and analytic quartic remainder. Sublevel ellipsoid volume, Jacobian 1/4, two ordered cap charts and exact surface-area normalization yield 1/[4a(a+r)] and O(epsilon^3). The sphere formula follows from a uniform directional dot product. In the moving a=lambda epsilon regime angular-cap integration and cylinder negligibility give Psi(lambda) after bounded convergence; differentiation gives the C1/C2 claim, and algebra gives reconstruction. An independent exact-coordinate angular quadrature script passed 35 tests; it does not prove the infinite claims.

value.rationale: The naturally motivated random-surface chord observable sharply changes its tail exponent under arbitrarily slight capsule elongation. A complete nontrivial, piecewise smooth critical crossover resolves this nonuniform singular limit, the unique critical lambda=1/2 has a second-derivative jump, and the fixed tail coefficient plus diameter recovers an unknown capsule shape. These are nontrivial geometric-probability phenomena beyond the elementary sphere CDF.
